text:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: sustained HTTP error-rate increase on ingress-eu-west1 (window=3m). 502/503s up ~18% vs baseline. Trigger: latency+5xx rule. PagerDuty incident INC-7421 created and paged oncall.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INCIDENT INC-7421 — Acknowledgement required. Escalation policy: primary -> secondary in 6m.

Maya: acked. I’m on it — looking at traffic slice and recent deploys. :eyes:

Amanda: thanks. any customer impact yet? metrics show increased 5xx but upstream responses look varied.

CJ: quick sanity check: was there a config push ~11:30? I see a small nginx-ingress config change in git at 11:27 from infra-ryan.

Ryan: that was a benign header tweak for X-Request-ID routing; rolled out via canary, shouldn't affect codepaths but could alter sticky routing.

Maya: grabbing logs from gateway pods. running: `kubectl -n infra logs -l app=ingress-gateway --tail=200` to kickoff. also hitting `/healthz` on a few pods.

Maya: logs show repeated backend timeouts + 502s. Snippet:
```
[2025-06-03T11:39:12Z] upstream timed out (110) while reading response header from upstream
[2025-06-03T11:39:13Z] 502 while reading response from upstream
[2025-06-03T11:39:14Z] upstream prematurely closed connection
```

Amanda: that looks like upstream (kvcache / inference sidecar) instability. could be connection exhaustion.

CJ: can we reproduce with a quick curl through the gateway? `curl -vv \"https://ingress-eu.example/api/health\" -H 'Host: model.redwood'` — if we get 502 from multiple nodes it's systemic.

Maya: doing the curl now. getting intermittent 200/502 depending on node. mapping to pods -> pod-3 and pod-7 show high connection resets.

Maya: running `kubectl top pod -n workloads` — pod-3 CPU spiking and open fd count is high. suspect file descriptor saturation on the upstream service.

Ryan: fallthrough: try draining traffic from affected nodes. We can remove pods from service LB for a slice and let autoscaler spin replacements.

CJ: follow runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ingress-upstream-5xx|Ingress upstream 5xx runbook> step 2 suggests `kubectl annotate svc ingress-gateway redwood/drain=true` to splay traffic. we usually use the rollout-slice technique.

Maya: doing a controlled drain of 20% slice: `kubectl label node node-aws-eu-west1a redwood/drain-slice=1` then patch service weights. I'll apply to two nodes first.

Maya: applied slice drain to node-aws-eu-west1a/1 and node-aws-eu-west1b/2. Watching error-rate.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-7421 acknowledged by Maya. Escalation timer paused.

Amanda: error-rate dropped to +6% within 90s after slice drain. still seeing occasional 502s but much lower. good signal that traffic concentration was the issue.

CJ: next step: confirm if the kvcache sidecar has a leaking connection pool. can we restart the kvcache pods one-by-one in the affected slice?

Maya: scheduling rolling restart of kvcache for the drained slice: `kubectl -n ml rollout restart statefulset/kvcache --selector=redwood/drain-slice=1` — restarting sequentially.

Maya: restarts done. pods came up healthy. metrics show successful connections back to upstream.

Amanda: ok to widen slice back to normal and monitor, or do we keep thin drain and continue profiling?

CJ: keep monitoring 10m before full reintegration. also capture pprof from kvcache for root cause. I'll open an eval job.

Luke: I'm taking oncall handoff in 45m. if it still looks unstable at handoff I'll take over mitigation and initiate a hotfix to connection pooling config.

Maya: noted. I'll leave the slice at 20% and a dashboard watch. Added a short-term alert: increase 5xx threshold to avoid noisy paging while we stabilize.

Amanda: filing a customer-impact note for SRE->CS: approx 0.4% of requests experienced 502/503 in eu-west1 between 11:36-11:42. No major customers reported degradations yet. Drafting message now.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-7421 — Status updated: Mitigated (partial). Keep monitoring.

CJ: follow-ups: (1) postmortem to include root-cause of fd exhaustion; (2) add fd / connection pool health check to prod health endpoints; (3) consider circuit-breaker on gateway for flaky upstreams.

Maya: handing off to Luke at 12:25 UTC. leaving runbook notes and exact commands in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-7421

Luke: ack, I'll pick up monitoring and coordinate the postmortem if we confirm kvcache leak. will notify CS if the 10m window clears.

Amanda: thanks team. great rapid triage. :thumbsup:

Ryan: FYI I'll roll back the header tweak if we see any unusual routing persists, but current signal points to kvcache connection saturation rather than header behavior.

Maya: closing slack thread for now, will update when Luke confirms final state. leaving pagerduty incident open for postmortem tasks.

incident-bot: Incident INC-7421 — slack thread updated. runbook ref: ingress-upstream-5xx. resources: dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/ingress-eu/5xx-overview

Luke: final check at 12:34 UTC: error-rate stable at +1.2%; closing mitigation window. passing to postmortem queue.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-7421 — Incident resolved by Luke. Please follow postmortem process and add RCA.

Maya: thanks. adding a blameless RCA draft now.

Amanda: good job everyone. I'll follow up with a short customer notification draft for any partners who hit errors.
